summary: Marie-Stella Boussemart studied under Samten Gyaltsen Karmay and Dagpo Rinpoche.

Specializing in Indology, Buddhist studies, and history and archaeology, de Mallmann earned diplomas from École Pratique des Hautes Études and École du Louvre. She worked at CNRS (1942–1974) and was chargée de mission at Guimet Museum (1948–1975).

Marielle Harrison, a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies, studied at the University of Washington and the University of Chicago (MA attested 2026). She served as a Teaching Fellow at Chicago (2025–2026) and postdoctoral fellow lecturer at Stanford (2026).

Mariia Lepneva, working in Buddhist studies and sinology, earned an MA from MGIMO and studied in the PhD program at Buryat State University (2015–2021). She became a postdoctoral researcher at Ghent University (2023–2026).

Marijan Molé, a specialist in Iranian, Central Asian, and religious studies, completed his PhD at Jagiellonian University and a diploma at EPHE. He held posts at Jagiellonian University, CNRS (1950–1955), IFRI (1955–1959), and EPHE (~1955–1963).

Marilyn Hirsh, who worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and history and archaeology, studied at Carnegie Mellon University (~1961–1965). She taught Indian and Buddhist art at Cooper Union and the Institute of Fine Arts, New York University.
Marina Illich, a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, completed her PhD at Columbia University by 2006 under the supervision of Robert A. F. Thurman.

Marina Rimscha, an Indologist and linguist, earned an M.A. and Dr. Phil. from the University of Bonn. She held positions at the University of Haifa (2016–2021) and as a lecturer at Technion (2025–2026).

Mario Bonardi worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology, studying under Giuseppe Tucci (~1933–1938) and Carlo Formichi. He held posts at Sapienza University of Rome (~1945–1954) and the Italian Institute for Africa and the East (~1947–1954).

Mario Bussagli, who worked in history, archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology, completed his dissertation under Giuseppe Tucci at Sapienza University of Rome (~1936–1940), where he later served as docent (1957–1987).

Mario Cappieri worked in Indology and history and archaeology. He was a lecturer in demography at Sapienza University of Rome (~1950–1964) and professor of anthropology at the University of Naples Federico II in 1955.

Mario D'Amato, specializing in Buddhist studies and philosophy, earned his PhD at the University of Chicago under Paul J. Griffiths (~1994–2000). He served as assistant professor of philosophy and religion at Rollins College (~2000–2006).

Mario Daza de Campos was an Indologist who studied under Francisco García Ayuso and taught Pedro Urbano González de la Calle. He served as ordinary professor of Sanskrit at Complutense University of Madrid (~1912–1933).

Mario Poceski, specializing in Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies, completed his PhD at UCLA under Robert E. Buswell Jr. in 2000. In 2001, he joined the University of Florida as assistant professor.
Mario Praz studied at the universities of Bologna (~1914–1918) and Florence (~1918–1920). He held posts at the University of Manchester (~1932–1934) and Sapienza University of Rome (~1934–1966).
Mario Vallauri, working in Indology and linguistics, studied at Naples, Florence, and Würzburg. He served as libero docente (1922) and lecturer in Sanskrit (1924–1931) at the University of Turin.

Marion L. Matics, who worked in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology, earned a PhD at Columbia University (1960) under Horace L. Friess. He taught Oriental philosophy at Columbia University and Brooklyn College.

Marion Meyer, a scholar of history and archaeology, completed her Ph.D. at the University of Bonn (1975–1984). She served as associate professor at Bonn (1997–2003) and full professor at the University of Vienna (2003–2020).

Marion Rastelli, a scholar of Indology and religious studies, completed doctoral studies under Gerhard Oberhammer. She held an affiliation with the Austrian Academy of Sciences (attested 2019) and served as a lecturer at the University of Vienna (attested 2020–2026).
Marius Zemp, a linguist and Tibetologist, earned his Lizentiat at the University of Bern (1999–2014) and later served there as a lecturer (2020–2025).
